Use the Stryker C++ source tree and current main branch. Review mutation testing behavior, CLI compatibility, and workflow/config changes conservatively. Focus on parity with Stryker's C# / .NET conventions and local review findings.

Stryker.NET, the .NET mutation testing tool (upstream). Review conservatively: the repo's own CONTRIBUTING + .github/instructions (conventional-commit, csharp, security-and-owasp, self-explanatory-code-commenting) are authoritative. Focus on the analyzer-config / source-generator bug classes - a generator that silently emits nothing must not be misattributed as a mutation or internal Stryker error - plus rollback correctness and whether unit tests actually exercise the changed branches. Squash-merge only.

Personal skill and plugin repository — LOCAL review only. Apply the checkout README and review lifecycle changes conservatively. For Issue Loop, enforce fail-closed publication, sanitized persistence, duplicate-aware reporting, stable runtime convergence, and transactional watcher rollback. Never auto-close or comment from local review.

Our own diff-scoped, fail-closed property/invariant testing PR-gate CLI (marmorkrebs sibling; fast-check lane, JS/.mjs). Review fail-closed semantics hard: a tool failure, empty run, or QUARANTINED engine must never read as a pass, and property/invariant modules must be authored per behavior-changing PR, not assumed present.

Our own PR-scoped multi-language mutation orchestrator (TS/node CLI dispatching stryker/mutmut/cargo-mutants/gomu/stryker-net/stryker-cxx). Review fail-open hardest: any path where a tool failure, missing binary, kill signal, zero-mutant run, or unparseable report reads as a passing/score-1.0 result is a P1; reconcileResult is the net and changes must not route around it. Adapter or parser edits are invalid without live real-tool evidence (validate-provider lane PASS). Enforce node 20/22 x ubuntu/macos/windows portability: no shell-glob or quoting assumptions, no exit-code-through-pipe, platform-agnostic paths in tests.

Our own diff-scoped, fail-closed CONCURRENCY PR-gate CLI (marmorkrebs/einsiedlerkrebs sibling, TS/node). LOCAL review only; never auto-close or comment. Review fail-closed semantics hard: a lane may not score unless it caught its planted-race fixture THIS run, and a tool failure, empty run, timeout misclassification, or lane-dead verdict must never read as a pass. Detector/probe edits are invalid without a passing validate:detector lane (planted race caught+anchored, clean fixture clean, toolchain-hidden fails closed). Apply the repo's own AGENTS.md/README as the review contract.

steipete's Swift macOS menu-bar AI-usage tracker (UPSTREAM, not ours). This review vets a concurrency fix surfaced by signalkrebs (swift-tsan). Judge whether the lock-based fix is the BEST solution: correct (no deadlock — note the setter recomputes the mirror via the isDisabled getter under the lock, hence NSRecursiveLock), minimal, behavior-preserving, and idiomatic to the repo (matches the existing NSLock sibling). Flag any simpler/safer approach (e.g. Swift Mutex, a lock-held helper vs recursive lock).

External upstream reviewed locally only. Apply pikvm/kvmd's current README, workflow, setup.py, and EditorConfig plus the local kvmd additions contract. For kvmd-localhid changes, review evdev capability classification, per-device key filtering, unsupported-key handling, keyboard/mouse regressions, and exact real-device base-versus-HEAD evidence. Never auto-close, comment, push, or create an issue or PR.

External kernel.org maintainer tree, reviewed locally only. The Linux in-tree process and coding-assistant policies are authoritative. Review USB gadget descriptor correctness, standards-required bcdUSB minima, unset/default behavior, configfs compatibility, and exact base-versus-HEAD host observations. Never auto-close, comment, push, or send email.
Windows companion suite (C#/.NET 10, WinUI 3). Upstream (openclaw-owned) — per-PR approval. Base ref origin/main. AGENTS.md is the base contract.

Use the crabfleet source tree and current main branch. Cloudflare Workers + D1 node-lifecycle worker: review with the concurrency lens -- D1 has no cross-invocation serialization, so check-then-act across an await can interleave with concurrent requests, cron scheduled() handlers, and reconcilers (guard-asymmetry: a sibling path guards it, this path forgot). Upstream/conservative: do NOT auto-close issues or pull requests.

Use the Peekaboo source tree and current main branch. Swift 6.2 MCP/CLI automation tool. Review MCP tool trust-boundary and path-confinement changes with high rigor (model-controlled tool arguments are untrusted). Keep everything open for maintainer triage; do not propose auto-close.
